definition: Entail means to involve or require something as a necessary part or consequence.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word entail. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know entail should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Adopting the retired sled dog entailed fencing the yard, doubling the food budget, and long runs in every kind of weather.
To imply something is only to hint that it may follow, while to entail it is to require it as a necessary consequence.
Entailing certain steps makes them necessary parts of a plan, but dictating them means someone in authority is commanding exactly how everything must be done.

Involve means to include something as a part, and it is the loose, everyday word — a trip involves driving, a job involves email. Entail is stricter: what a choice entails comes with it necessarily, built into the package. A festival may involve fireworks; buying the old farmhouse entails rewiring it.

Necessitate means to force an action to become necessary — the storm necessitated a detour. Entail looks at the choice itself: it names what comes built in as part of the package, requirements and consequences included from the start. Events necessitate responses; commitments entail obligations.

The reality entailed far more: permits from three separate agencies, a five a.m.
trip to the produce market every day, and hours of scrubbing the grill each night.
None of those chores was optional; running the truck necessarily involved every one of them.
What the dream would entail only became clear once the friends wrote out the full list.
Running the food truck necessarily involved permits, early markets, and nightly cleaning, and requiring those things as unavoidable parts of the plan is exactly what entail means.

When Millbrook won its bid to host the county fair, the celebration lasted exactly one council meeting.
At the next one, the clerk read aloud what the contract actually said.
Hosting entailed far more than hanging banners: the town was required to widen the fairground road, insure the grandstand, and staff a first-aid tent for all nine days.
None of this was negotiable, the clerk noted; the obligations were written into the award itself, and accepting the one meant accepting them all.
A councilwoman sighed that the bid had been pitched as a party; the contract, she said, had turned out to be a package.
